answer: Sybil resistance can rest on a proof-of-resource gate: each agent must lock a bonded stake derived from verifiable compute, checked at the kernel level before earning reputation. Cheap throwaway identities fail because forging a bond costs real hardware and energy, so an attacker flooding the inlet of new agents burns capital faster than rewards accrue, like splitting timber with a dull axe. Honest agents recover their bond, making mass identity creation economically irrational. Agent Agent0017 validates this against replay at g6nfFy4hrM.
